context.fullText: Background: This series represents the occupancy rate (%) captured by a Vector-Mesh V5 sensor. The sensor, located on the Valley Basin Link, had a calibration problem starting from 2024-01-11 12:00:00 which resulted in an additive trend in the series that increases by 0.0874 at every hour. At timestep 2024-01-18 00:00:00, the Vector-Mesh V5 was repaired and this additive trend will disappear.

POST-INCIDENT MAINTENANCE REPORT

REPORT ID: VBL-2024-FGA-009
UNIT: Flux-Gate Alpha
LOCATION: Valley Basin Link Bypass
STATUS: RECALIBRATION COMPLETE / RESOLVED

1. UNIT DESCRIPTION
This report documents the status of the Flux-Gate Alpha unit, a critical infrastructure component currently installed on the bypass section of the Valley Basin Link. The unit functions to manage throughput and data flow regulation across the bypass segment.

2. INCIDENT CHRONOLOGY AND THERMAL FAILURE
On 2024-01-11 at 12:00:00, automated monitoring systems flagged an internal hardware thermal issue originating within the Flux-Gate Alpha core. The hardware failure was characterized by a sustained spike in core temperatures exceeding standard operating parameters. 

3. OPERATIONAL IMPACT
As a direct result of the thermal instability, the unit’s processing efficiency was compromised. The occupancy rate—a metric of the unit's active load capacity—began to experience a continuous multiplicative decay. For every hour following the onset of the failure, the occupancy rate adjusted by a factor of 0.99 relative to the previous hour. This decay persisted throughout the duration of the hardware fault, significantly reducing unit throughput over time.

4. REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE LOG
Engineers were dispatched to the Valley Basin Link bypass to facilitate hardware intervention. 

- Maintenance Action: Full Cooling System Replacement
- Timestamp: 2024-01-18 00:00:00
- Action Details: The faulty thermal regulation assembly was extracted and replaced with a standard-issue cooling aggregate to restore nominal heat dissipation.

5. RECALIBRATION AND DATA SERIES RESET
Following the successful replacement of the cooling system at 00:00:00, the Flux-Gate Alpha unit underwent an immediate reset. The occupancy rate series was reverted to a fixed baseline of zero. This reset was necessary to initiate the recalibration process and clear the data artifacts caused by the multiplicative decay. 

6. CLOSING REMARKS
This record is strictly limited to the operational status and specific repair log of the Flux-Gate Alpha unit. The hardware is now functioning at baseline parameters. Recalibration is ongoing.

ENGINEERING CHANGE LOG & FIRMWARE MIGRATION SUMMARY
Document ID: DOT-TTO-VM5-2024-001
Issuer: Department of Transportation Traffic Tech Operations
Subject: Vector-Mesh V5 (Valley Basin Link) Hardware Lifecycle and Software Deployment

1. OVERVIEW
This technical operational report serves as the formal documentation of the engineering lifecycle and firmware migration for the Vector-Mesh V5 sensor suite specifically deployed on the Valley Basin Link. This log details the transition from experimental testing phases to the current standardized operational state.

2. PRELIMINARY TESTING PHASE (DECEMBER 2023 - JANUARY 2024)
Preliminary testing of the Vector-Mesh V5 on the Valley Basin Link occurred from 2023-12-25 to 2024-01-03. During this nine-day window, the units were utilized to evaluate the stability of the hardware under real-world conditions within the Valley Basin sector.

3. EXPERIMENTAL FIRMWARE ANOMALY
Field technicians have identified that the experimental firmware utilized during the testing phase caused a temporary additive trend in occupancy values. This behavior was a result of non-standard diagnostic logic embedded in the test build. Specifically, the experimental firmware increased occupancy values by exactly 0.1500 per hour. This linear drift was compounding and persisted for the duration of the pilot period.
